# Solution design assessment

## Evidence and scope

- Full pinned story: `user_story`, `characters 0-16000`. Build a Python 3.12 Flask, server-rendered password-reset prototype with pytest, synthetic accounts, an in-memory notification sink and documented production limitations. Do not deploy or add deployment workflows.
- Supplied image: attachment `23b23ac1-a532-42fc-9973-51a1d4954aa6`, `sign-in-wireframe.png`. I observed a white 480 x 360 canvas with a narrow, horizontally centered dark-bordered panel; a bold "Sign in" heading; labeled "Email address" field with `name@example.com` placeholder; labeled masked "Password" field; blue underlined "Forgot password?" link; wide dark "Sign in" button; and muted "No account? Contact your administrator." footer. The image establishes visible presentation, not functioning sign-in or recovery screens.
- Approved prior outputs read via the stage-output service: `requirements_analysis` (REQ-001 through REQ-018), `ui_analysis` (observed sign-in details distinguished from proposed recovery states), and `acceptance_20261025121757_621df1_risk` (12 prospective risks, not measured defects). The service provided stage keys and JSON text, but no standalone source-reference locator for those outputs: cite their requirement IDs as predecessor links, not fabricated `stage_output` source references.
- Curated account recovery standard: knowledge source `bcf198d8-a628-401c-8641-b726fcbd00b5`, `v1, chunk 0`. ACC-STD-01 requires a recovery link, identical existing/unknown request responses and a five-per-account-per-hour limit; ACC-STD-02 requires single-use links expiring at 30 minutes and all-session sign-out after reset; ACC-STD-03 requires an owner notification after each successful reset. A targeted architecture-policy search found no separate applicable organizational guidance beyond duplicate copies of this standard; do not infer other approved technology or hosting policy.
- Repository inspection found the prior SDLC documents and a minimal README, with no application implementation, tests, packaging, or existing build/test/lint commands to reuse. No deployment work is authorized.

## Design implications and evidence gaps

All 18 approved requirements need explicit implementation-task or justified disposition coverage. In particular, plan for sign-in presentation/entry (REQ-001/002), privacy and per-account throttling (003/004), in-memory link issuance (005/011/012), single use and exact expiry boundary (006/007), password replacement, invalidation of *every* active session, and owner notification (008-010), Flask/Python/server rendering (013-015), automated pytest verification (016), honest limitations (017), and no deployment/workflow (018). Keep the task dependency graph acyclic and stable `TASK-NNN` identifiers.

The email shown in the image is the presumed recovery identifier; no recovery-page mockup, sign-in authentication behavior, password-strength policy, session technology, persistence provider, external notification provider, or production deployment design is specified. Those remain design choices or open questions, not observed facts. The approved UI analysis proposes recovery screens and accessibility/error states but does not make them pictured requirements. Design must address token handling, authentication/session invalidation, data privacy, reliability, observability and testable time boundaries without implying production readiness. Validate account-independent visitor-facing response independently of internal sink contents; do not expose test-only links on public pages.

Phase 1 only: no product output, production code, or plan has been written. Subsequent planning requires approval before document execution.
